_: Vendored-file manifest for oc-vendor-drift (issue #700). Each entry names a file this repo carries a copy of, the upstream revision it was flattened from, and the ONLY differences permitted. A delta entry matches OUR form via `match` and THEIR form via `match_upstream` (defaulting to `match`), because a delta line must be droppable from both sides or the comparison shifts. Anything else is drift and fails the guard.

vendor.why: Vendored copy of the Open Questions register. The delta below is the DEPLOYMENT difference only. Re-flattened at c2856ad (#44): the #497 vocabulary widening is now declared as BLOCK deltas because its lines are not unique (a bare '#' and blank lines recur), and a per-line pattern broad enough to name them would strip unrelated lines and stop the guard discriminating -- the #41 trap. A block is an EXACT contiguous run stripped from its OWN side only; zero or two occurrences is DRIFTED, never a silent pass (#343).

This copy read the session id ALONE, so every such caller was logged as actor="unknown" and could not be traced to a lane. Upstream ask: the same one line.

The C6 mechanical-closure probe's default tracker. A factory question's work unit is filed on the FACTORY tracker, so probing the fork for it answers about a repo that unit is not filed on -- a confident, WRONG 'still open'. Defaults to the factory tracker; OC_QUESTIONS_TRACKER still overrides. (The fork is a real tracker again since the 2026-10-08 re-scope, but only for FORK-ONLY defects -- never the default for a factory question.) UPSTREAM ASK: flip the same default in TEMPLATE/tools/questions.

Close REASON: it hardcoded the word 'fork' while the probe now asks the factory tracker, so the message a lane reads would name the wrong repo. Interpolating the constant makes the reason state its own scope -- '<slug>#N is CLOSED' (rule: a number travels with its predicate and scope). UPSTREAM ASK: same fix in TEMPLATE/tools/questions.

block: # A question is CLOSED once it is answered, withdrawn, expired, or closed by a
# predicate. "clarifying" is NOT closed: a Clarify request means the owner asked
# for more context and is still waiting. Counting it as closed archived the WHOLE
# set and silently removed it from the live register — the opposite of the
# contract ("a Clarify request ... never silently closes the question").
# "resolved_mechanically" BELONGS HERE and was missing (#497). The mechanical
# writer in `apply_mechanical_closures` stamps that status TOGETHER with
# `closed_at` and `closed_reason` — a CLOSED row by every other measure — while
# this tuple, which `question_is_closed` is a plain membership test on, did not
# name it. One omission, three readers wrong at once: the predicate said False,
# so `set_is_closed` could never archive a mechanically-resolved set (its last
# question never read as closed), and `cmd_answer`'s idempotent-by-contract guard
# never fired, letting a resolved question be FLIPPED to `answered` by a
# re-submit instead of being refused with rc 3. The law settles which side is
# wrong — `docs/instruments/open-questions.md` §3: "Closure is mechanical
# wherever it can be" — so the vocabulary is widened, not the writer changed.
# ONE constant, because every reader derives from it: no reader-local special
# case, no second list (#494's class, applied to closure).
CLOSED_STATUSES = ("answered", "withdrawn", "expired", "resolved_mechanically")
delta.why: local-only patch at residual line 781 (20 lines, 0 context)

block: # A question is CLOSED only once it is answered, withdrawn or expired.
# "clarifying" is NOT closed: a Clarify request means the owner asked for more
# context and is still waiting. Counting it as closed archived the WHOLE set and
# silently removed it from the live register — the opposite of the contract
# ("a Clarify request ... never silently closes the question").
CLOSED_STATUSES = ("answered", "withdrawn", "expired")
delta.why: upstream form replaced at residual line 781 (6 lines, 0 context)

block: # -- 8e. #497: the closed vocabulary NAMES the status the mechanical
# writer writes. `apply_mechanical_closures` stamps `resolved_mechanically`
# together with `closed_at` and `closed_reason` -- a closed row by every
# other measure -- while CLOSED_STATUSES, which `question_is_closed` is a
# plain membership test on, did not name it. One omission, three readers
# wrong at once, so the legs below are the three readers plus the control.
ck(question_is_closed({"status": "resolved_mechanically"}),
"question_is_closed reads a mechanically-resolved row as CLOSED (#497)")
# The set predicate is the second reader, and it is what `gc` consults
# before it flips a fully-closed set. A set of ONE mechanically-resolved
# question was never closed, so the set stayed `open` forever.
ck(set_is_closed({"questions": [{"status": "resolved_mechanically"}]}),
"\u2026and set_is_closed reads a mechanically-resolved set as CLOSED")
ck(get_set(mech_set).get("status") == "answered",
"\u2026so gc marks the set itself answered once every question is "
"closed (status=%r)" % (get_set(mech_set) or {}).get("status"))
# The third reader is `cmd_answer`'s idempotent-by-contract guard. It must
# REFUSE (rc 3) and leave the row untouched -- not flip it to `answered`.
rc, out, _ = run("answer", mech_set, "q1", "0")
ck(rc == 3, "a re-submit on a mechanically-resolved question is REFUSED, "
"idempotent-by-contract (rc=%d)" % rc)
ck(get_set(mech_set)["questions"][0]["status"] == "resolved_mechanically",
"\u2026and the row keeps its status instead of being flipped to "
"answered (%r)" % get_set(mech_set)["questions"][0]["status"])
# THE POSITIVE CONTROL. A fix that widened the guard to refuse everything
# would pass every leg above, so the three statuses that were ALREADY in
# the vocabulary must keep reading closed, and the three that were never
# closed must keep reading open. The vocabulary was WIDENED, not replaced.
for _closed in ("answered", "withdrawn", "expired"):
ck(question_is_closed({"status": _closed}),
"\u2026and the pre-existing status %r still reads CLOSED" % _closed)
for _open in ("open", "clarifying", "clarified"):
ck(not question_is_closed({"status": _open}),
"\u2026while %r still reads NOT closed, so the guard was widened "
"rather than made to refuse everything" % _open)
